# OpenJarvisProject

> A generic, FOSS, local-first Jarvis-like AI agent for Linux and
> Android. Runs on the user's own hardware, each device its own full
> offline-capable instance, with a shared "second brain" memory
> database synced peer-to-peer across devices without a required
> central server. Early planning stage: no code exists yet, this repo
> documents architecture decisions as they're made.

This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention: a
flat, link-based index for AI agents/tools reading this repo, so a
coding agent can find the relevant doc directly instead of reading
everything. Each doc below is self-contained and states what's decided
vs. still open — don't infer certainty beyond what a doc actually
claims.

## Core

- [README.md](README.md): project summary, repo layout, current status
- [vision.md](vision.md): what this is, why it exists, naming and
  persona/branding model, relationship to the prior ZELIA project

## Architecture

- [architecture/runtime.md](architecture/runtime.md): Rust app layer +
  C++ (`llama.cpp`) inference kernels + `burn.dev` fallback role;
  staged validation methodology; open question on pruning-tooling
  language (Python/PyTorch vs. all-Rust)
- [architecture/model-compression.md](architecture/model-compression.md):
  pruning/factorization/quantization/offloading/router-specialist
  strategy, target model sizes, the pruning→publishing pipeline, and
  real target hardware specs
- [architecture/sync-and-devices.md](architecture/sync-and-devices.md):
  per-device offline instances (not client-server), CRDT-based
  (Automerge + Iroh) second-brain memory sync, LAN-discovery-is-not-
  auth security model, zero-GMS requirement on Android, assistant-role
  integration
- [architecture/cloud-hosting.md](architecture/cloud-hosting.md):
  planned optional paid cloud tier (self-hosted, donation-funded,
  no-log privacy pitch) and its unresolved operational/legal risks

## Process

- [specs.md](specs.md): relationship between this repo, the planned
  `OJPs` spec repo, and MCP (adopted for agent-to-tool invocation
  specifically, not a replacement for OJPs)
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to propose changes
